clue.text: Untrue earth's damaged in game offering prize?

indicators.note: damaged letters are knocked out of shape, so the words before it are rearranged

parts.note: read as earth has, so the S counts as a letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: A false claim about the planet has been spoilt in a contest with a reward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges UNTRUE plus EARTHS (earth's read as 'earth has', keeping its S), twelve letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: A search game with clues leading to a hidden reward is a classic party pursuit; the question mark flags the loose description.

clue.text: Diplomatic account defended by dry female, university lecturer

indicators.note: something defended by another is surrounded and protected by it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: TT, teetotal, is a dry person who drinks no alcohol

explanation.surface: A diplomat's account is guarded by a sober woman who lectures at a university.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone diplomatic handles people with tact and sensitivity, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: English bachelor staying in mean joint

indicators.note: a guest staying in a house is inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: low means mean or base in character

explanation.surface: An unmarried Englishman lives in a stingy rented room.
explanation.definitionFit: The arm's middle hinge is a joint of the body, an example of the category.

clue.text: Past railway containing appeal and no fake feeling

parts.note: since means past, as in 'two years since'

indicators.note: containing means holding something within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: IT is crossword shorthand for sex appeal

explanation.surface: An old railway line holds charm and real emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Genuineness of emotion, feeling that is not put on, is the quality of honesty described.

clue.text: Republican period brought up? Not common

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing a word up makes it read from bottom to top

parts.note: an era is a period of history

explanation.surface: A political party's era is raised again: an unusual event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns ERA into ARE beneath R, as this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not common is scarce or seldom found, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Tree with worth cultivated among Chinese people

indicators.note: among means in the midst of, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the Han are the majority ethnic group of China

indicators.note: cultivated soil is worked over, so the letters of the next word are turned around

explanation.surface: A valuable tree is grown in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cultivated' gives AWTHOR; the Han are China's majority people, so 'Chinese people' is not a generic plural.
explanation.definitionFit: This thorny shrub with white May blossom is a common small tree of hedgerows.

clue.text: Hospital in French city offering comfortable place?

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: Nice is a city on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: A hospital on the Riviera offers a pleasant spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a position where one fits snugly, a suitable comfortable spot; the question mark marks the figurative sense.

clue.text: Old coin, distant object

parts.note: far means distant
a thing is an object

explanation.surface: An old coin is a remote item, lost long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: This quarter-penny piece was a British coin until 1961, so an old coin by example.

clue.text: Publicity in church for pop musician

parts.note: PR, public relations, is publicity
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Publicity inside a church for a pop star.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince was the American singer behind Purple Rain, an example of a pop musician.

clue.text: Company initially incorporated in a drink staff on board?

indicators.note: initially signals taking just the opening letter of the word before it
in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: brew is a drink, especially of tea or beer

explanation.surface: A firm starts by being incorporated in a pub serving beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Flight attendants are the staff working aboard an aircraft, hence those on board.

clue.text: Official companion getting appearance

parts.note: CH is Companion of Honour, a British order
an air is a manner or appearance

explanation.surface: A companion is given a certain look.
explanation.definitionFit: A chair is the person presiding over a meeting, an official who conducts business.

clue.text: Lexicographer of more unpleasant disposition, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: fouler means nastier, of a more unpleasant disposition

explanation.surface: A dictionary writer with a rather nastier temperament, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: H. W. Fowler wrote Modern English Usage and co-edited the Concise Oxford Dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Fowler compiled dictionaries and usage guides, so he is a famous example of a dictionary maker.

clue.text: Short time weaving near the loom

parts.note: T is the shortened form of time

indicators.note: weaving moves strands in and out, so the words after it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A brief period spent weaving next to a loom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weaving' rearranges NEAR THE into HREATEN after T. 'Loom' is the verb here, not the weaving frame the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To loom is to appear as a menacing prospect, the verb sense matching to menace.

clue.text: Lieutenant skirts a Roman road in country

indicators.note: skirts means goes around the edge of, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: via is Latin for road, as in the Via Appia

explanation.surface: An officer goes round a Roman highway on his way into a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Latvia is a Baltic state, an example of a country.

clue.text: Excessively describing seismologist's research trip?

definitions.meaning: the phrase means too much, beyond reason, as in generous to an extreme
an earthquake scientist would travel to a crack in the earth's crust

explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' links the two senses; the second reads the phrase literally as a journey to a geological fracture.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to an excessive degree, while literally it is a destination for earthquake study.

clue.text: Standing pier gets demolished

indicators.note: a demolished structure is broken up, so the letters of the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pier is torn down.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing in society means status or reputation, a synonym of renown.

clue.text: Young male professionally engaged in stalls?

definitions.text: Young male professionally engaged in stalls?

parts.words: Young male professionally engaged in stalls?
parts.note: the stalls are not theatre seats but compartments for horses, where a youth works as a groom

explanation.definitionFit: A youth employed at a racing yard to care for horses works among their stalls.

clue.text: Sweet office worker, calm and with energy

parts.note: a PA is a personal assistant in an office
still means calm
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A lovely secretary, composed and full of vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fruit-flavoured lozenge is a type of confectionery, an example of a sweet.

clue.text: Male has trained around yard dog

indicators.note: around means one piece encircles another
trained means put into a new shape, so the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man has drilled a hound about the yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' gives SEALHAM. The Sealyham is a Welsh terrier breed, so 'dog' is the definition, not a part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: This Welsh terrier breed is named after a Pembrokeshire estate, an example of a dog.

clue.text: Almost take action against man being overly sentimental

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to sue is to take legal action against someone
Gary is a man's name

explanation.surface: Nearly suing a man for being too soppy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugary describes something cloyingly sweet in feeling, mawkish and excessively sentimental.

clue.text: Suspend inhibition

definitions.meaning: to suspend is to hang something from above

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to hang from a hook; as a noun it is a nagging emotional problem.

clue.text: Author not half enthralled by positive Roman writer of old

indicators.note: enthralled by means held captive inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: plus means positive

indicators.note: not half of the word means only its first half is kept

explanation.surface: A writer is half captivated by an optimistic Roman author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' keeps the first three of six letters. Plautus was a Roman comic playwright, c. 254 to 184 BC.
explanation.definitionFit: Plautus wrote comic plays in ancient Rome, so he is an example of a classical author.

clue.text: Good artist, fellow appropriate to lead one drawing on wall

indicators.note: to lead places the previous piece in front of the next

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
fit means suitable or appropriate
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A fine painter is the right one to create a wall mural.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing or pictures scrawled on public walls are an example of unofficial drawing.

clue.text: Official turns up around nine, dodgy figure?

indicators.note: around means one piece surrounds another
in a down clue, turning a word up reads it from bottom to top

parts.note: a ref is a referee, a sports official
IX is nine in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A referee arrives at about nine, a shady character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' gives FER, read upwards in this down entry. The question mark marks 'dodgy figure' as a description rather than a dictionary sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who arranges things by underhand means is a shady operator, hence a dodgy figure.

clue.text: Animal better reared in a US city

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles

indicators.note: reared means brought up, turning the word back to front

parts.note: to cap is to better or outdo

explanation.surface: A creature is raised more successfully in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reared' gives PAC. 'Better' is a verb here, to outdo, not a comparative or a gambler.
explanation.definitionFit: This South American camelid, kept for its wool, is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Old German's point of view

definitions.meaning: one of a Germanic tribe that settled in early England
a perspective or slant on a subject

explanation.definitionFit: The tribe gave England its name, while the common noun means a particular viewpoint.

clue.text: Choking conditions beginning to scare cat

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that is taken

parts.note: mog is British slang for a cat

explanation.surface: A frightening start for a cat that cannot breathe.
explanation.definitionFit: Polluted fog that makes breathing hard is a choking atmospheric condition.

clue.text: Have break about lake in front of a cross

indicators.note: in front of places the pieces before the next ones in order

parts.note: re means about or concerning
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: Take a rest by the lake beside a crossroads.
explanation.definitionFit: To unwind and take things easy is to have a rest or break.

clue.text: Story about male accompanied by frivolous sort of publicity

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: a lie is a story, an untruth
light means frivolous, not serious

explanation.surface: A tale of a man with a flippant manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the public eye is a kind of attention or publicity, from the theatre spotlight.

clue.text: Part of course with man beset by wild dogs requiring emergency vehicle

parts.note: a green is part of a golf course

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so one piece goes inside another
wild means unruly, signalling the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Des is a man's name

explanation.surface: Part of a golf course where a man is surrounded by wild dogs needs an ambulance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' gives GODS. Green Goddess was the British army fire engine called out in emergencies such as firefighters' strikes.
explanation.definitionFit: These army fire engines served as standby emergency vehicles during strikes in Britain.
